headline: MAJOR FIND: DPM Metals Hits 713m at 2.52 g/t AuEq in Gold-Copper Porphyry Discovery Adjacent to Chelopech Mine
snippet: DPM Metals announced a high-grade porphyry discovery at its Brevene South licence in Bulgaria, with drillhole EX_BRESPO_03 intersecting 713 metres at 2.52 g/t AuEq (1.31 g/t Au and 1.16% Cu) roughly 1 km from the active Chelopech underground mine. The hole remains open downhole and DPM plans to submit a Commercial Discovery Certificate application by September 2026.

headline: NUCLEAR FUEL PUSH: Urenco USA to Expand America's Only Uranium Enrichment Plant by 50% in Multi-Billion Build
snippet: Urenco USA announced a multibillion-dollar expansion of its National Enrichment Facility in Eunice, New Mexico — the only commercial uranium enrichment plant in the U.S. — adding 2.1 million SWU of new centrifuge capacity and lifting output by nearly 50%, with first production from new cascades expected in 2032. Cameco (CCJ) and Energy Fuels (UUUU) shares surged on the announcement.

headline: 360 g/t SILVER at Nevada Junior: Excalibur Metals' Bellehelen Hit Sits Inside Broad 100m Mineralized Zone Open at Depth
snippet: Excalibur Metals (TSXV: EXCL) reported maiden drill results at its Bellehelen Silver-Gold Project in Nevada, with hole BH26001 cutting 360 g/t Ag and 2.03 g/t Au over 1.52m within a broader zone grading 16.7 g/t Ag and 0.10 g/t Au across 100.58 metres. Four of ten holes from the 3,122m program remain pending, and mineralization is open at depth.

headline: GOLDMAN LIFTS COPPER TARGET 10%: Chile Hits 23-Year Output Low, Citigroup Eyes $15,000/t Within 12 Months
snippet: Goldman Sachs raised its end-2026 LME copper target to $13,735/tonne from $12,465, citing a 640,000-tonne ex-U.S. market deficit as Chile's April production hit its worst level since 2002 — with Escondida output down 16% and Collahuasi down 11%. Citigroup is targeting $14,500/tonne near-term and $15,000 within a year on AI data-centre and energy-transition demand.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,400 IN JUNE: Iran War Premium Keeps Safe-Haven Bid Alive as Silver Tests $77
snippet: Gold is trading in the $4,436–$4,523/oz range in early June 2026, supported by persistent geopolitical risk from the U.S.-Iran conflict that began in March, even as prices remain well off January's $5,000+ peak. Silver is holding near $76–$77/oz with consensus forecasts pointing to an $80–$85 range by month-end.

headline: CHINA BALKS: Zijin's C$5.5B Allied Gold Takeover Stalled by NDRC Over Mali Exposure and Valuation
snippet: Zijin Gold and Allied Gold (TSX: AAUC) have extended their arrangement agreement's outside date to July 29, 2026 after China's National Development and Reform Commission raised concerns about the ~5% acquisition premium and jurisdiction risk in Mali, which accounts for roughly half of Allied's gold output. Canada's Investment Canada Act sign-off is complete; Chinese NDRC clearance is the last remaining hurdle.

headline: SEVENTH STRAIGHT QUARTERLY JUMP: China Rare Earth Concentrate Prices Surge 45% in Q2 2026
snippet: China Northern Rare Earth Group set Q2 2026 concentrate pricing at 38,804 yuan/tonne — a 45% jump quarter-over-quarter and the seventh consecutive quarterly increase since China reformed its pricing mechanism in 2023. Tight domestic inventories, sulfuric acid shortages, and Chinese EV manufacturers absorbing ~60% of domestic output are compounding the structural squeeze for Western buyers.

headline: GDX AT ALL-TIME HIGH: Gold Miners ETF Up 108% Year-Over-Year, Finally Outrunning the Metal
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) has returned 108% year-over-year and is trading at an all-time high, outperforming the S&P 500 by more than 80 percentage points as producers run industry-wide costs well below $2,000/oz against a $4,400+ gold price. GDXJ has delivered a 203% price return over the same period, validating the long-awaited re-rating of gold equities.

headline: STORAGE BOOM RESCUES LITHIUM: Battery Carbonate DOUBLED in Q1 2026 as Energy Storage Demand Jumps 55%
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate surged from ~$13,433 to $26,278/tonne in Q1 2026 — nearly doubling — as supply delays at Chinese lepidolite mines and Zimbabwe's export ban tightened the market just as AI data-centre buildouts lifted battery storage demand. Energy storage demand for lithium is forecast to grow 55% in 2026, following a 71% jump in 2025.

headline: DEAL WAVE: Mining M&A Hits $21.6B in Q1 2026, Up 34% Year-Over-Year as Critical Minerals Drive Consolidation
snippet: Global mining recorded 121 M&A transactions totalling $21.6 billion in Q1 2026, up from $16.1 billion in Q1 2025, as majors and governments raced to lock in critical mineral supply chains. Strategic partnerships combining private capital and government financing are emerging as the dominant deal structure, with 32% of deal-makers citing them as the preferred transaction form.
